name: Success confirmation
summary: The screen after a task is done: what happened in one line, the key details to keep, what happens next, and where to go from here.
use: after a form or flow that someone will want proof of (a payment, an order, a sent invoice, a booking)
a11y: When this screen replaces the form, move focus to its heading (it has tabindex -1 for that), so it is read first; the part never moves focus on its own. Details are a description list.
notes: Move focus to the heading when this screen replaces the form.

use_when: a multi-step flow or important form has finished
the person may need a reference or receipt
avoid_when: a small, quick change: a toast is enough (toast-undo)
nothing changed yet (the request is pending): say it's pending, not done

parts.name: title
parts.what: the heading: what happened, in plain words, as in “Invoice sent”

parts.name: message
parts.what: one or two sentences: what it means and what to do next, as in “Gorsedown Print will get INV-2042 by email in a ”

parts.name: details.value
parts.what: what the person typed, as in “$4,280.00”

parts.name: next
parts.what: what happens next, as in “We'll email you when they open it and when they ”

empty.how: Not applicable: this state screen shows no list of records.

loading.how: Not applicable: shown only after the task is done.

error.how: If the task failed, don't show this; return to the form with page-banners and the person's values kept.

disabled.how: No control here is ever disabled; each one always does something.

overflow.how: Long values such as email addresses break anywhere instead of overflowing.

long_text.how: Titles balance and body text wraps at word boundaries inside a capped measure.

keyboard: Focus moves to the heading when the screen appears
Tab then reaches View invoice and Send another
